scope: Public records review of PM CARES, political finance and disclosed BJP/RSS institutional connections. Seven case records; no claim of exhaustive coverage or discovery of secret wrongdoing.

cases.title: PM CARES: official administration and contested disclosure
cases.summary: The fund's official FAQ describes PMO administration and independent private audit. Access to its tax-exemption records has been litigated.
cases.finding: The Delhi High Court set aside a CIC disclosure direction on 22 January 2024, addressing the Income Tax Act route and the failure to hear PM CARES as a third party. These are disclosure restrictions; they do not establish misappropriation. The FY2024–25 statement reports ₹1,279.91 crore of in-year receipts, ₹0.88 crore of payments and ₹8,452.07 crore closing balances (rounded). Receipts include ₹324.66 crore returned by implementing agencies. These aggregates warrant tracing the returns and project commitments; they do not measure final beneficiary delivery.
cases.limitation: January 2026 reporting describes appeal-hearing remarks, not a newly verified final judgment. No later dispositive order was verified in this review. Public-authority status, tax-record disclosure and audit scope must remain separate questions.
cases.response: The official account says contributions are voluntary and there is no budgetary support. The FY2024–25 receipts-and-payments statement bears an auditor signature dated 7 August 2026. Two AI reviewers' transcriptions agree and both years reconcile arithmetically; the separate auditor report and notes were not in the downloaded file. Disclosure litigation is distinct from whether an audit exists.

hypotheses.question: Does limited publication prevent reconciliation of specific PM CARES expenditures with delivered relief?
hypotheses.prediction: A selected sanction cannot be traced across sanction, implementing agency, procurement, payment and delivery records, even after requesting available records from each public agency.
hypotheses.alternative: Records are distributed among implementing ministries or hospitals, and delivery reconciles when those sources are combined.
hypotheses.falsifier: A complete independently reproducible reconciliation for the selected expenditure, including discrepancies and resolutions, weakens the proposed transparency-failure mechanism.
hypotheses.records: Published annual receipts and payments; Scheme sanction letters; Implementing-agency utilization certificates; Procurement awards and delivery acceptance reports; Note 11 explaining implementing-agency refunds of ₹3,24,65,80,919 in FY2024–25; Project-level balances and commitments
nextSteps: Select one expenditure and one financial year before collecting records
Request agency-held documents through lawful public-record procedures
Publish the reconciliation and unresolved fields without treating a missing document as missing money

cases.title: PM CARES: foreign contributions under an explicit exemption
cases.summary: PM CARES officially states it is exempt from all provisions of FCRA 2010 and accepts overseas donations. That is a disclosed legal arrangement, not evidence of an illicit foreign channel.
cases.finding: The foreign-donor identities, acceptance screening and conflict checks needed to test policy-influence theories were not established by the public pages reviewed.
cases.limitation: The exemption notification and a donor-level foreign ledger were not retrieved. No named donor-to-government-favour inference is supported here.
cases.response: The official About page presents the foreign-contribution arrangement as consistent with PMNRF practice. Emergency fundraising is an ordinary explanation for accepting overseas support.

hypotheses.question: Are conflict-of-interest checks available for overseas donors who also seek Indian government decisions?
hypotheses.prediction: For a disclosed donor with a documented regulatory interest, acceptance and recusal records omit an applicable conflict review while a specific decision deviates from comparable cases.
hypotheses.alternative: Donations serve emergency relief, decision-making remains separate, and apparent proximity reflects routine diplomatic or commercial activity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Contemporaneous screening, recusal, independent decision reasons and comparable non-donor outcomes contradict the proposed influence mechanism.
hypotheses.records: FCRA exemption notification and conditions; Published donor disclosures and corporate annual reports; Trustee conflict policy and acceptance criteria; Dated regulatory or procurement decisions
nextSteps: Locate the exemption instrument before interpreting its scope
Use only publicly identified institutional donors
Test a specific decision against matched non-donor cases; do not infer a money transfer from organizational association

cases.title: PM CARES: CSR incentives and public-sector fundraising
cases.summary: Government records document a CSR incentive and active ministerial requests for PSU donations. The 2020 guidance treated PM CARES differently from Chief Minister relief funds while allowing State Disaster Management Authority support.
cases.finding: MCA's 11 April 2020 FAQ recognized PM CARES contributions as CSR, excluded the specified Chief Minister/State relief funds, and recognized State Disaster Management Authority contributions. A 31 March 2020 ministerial release sought the maximum possible PSU CSR contribution to PM CARES.
cases.limitation: The documented policy difference and official request do not prove coercion, diversion or party benefit. The 2020 guidance is a historical policy record, not a statement of every current CSR rule.
cases.response: The request was publicly justified by the pandemic and described employee contributions as voluntary. PM CARES permits PSU CSR while excluding contributions from budgetary sources; these categories should not be collapsed.

hypotheses.question: Did the policy incentive materially displace previously planned local CSR relief?
hypotheses.prediction: After the March 2020 request, committed local projects at affected PSUs show larger cancellations or delays than comparable projects after accounting for pandemic shutdowns and profit changes.
hypotheses.alternative: Companies used uncommitted balances, added emergency expenditure or substituted centrally coordinated relief without reducing completed local assistance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Board-approved project histories show no attributable reduction in promised local delivery, or similar changes occur among matched non-donating firms.
hypotheses.records: PSU board and CSR committee approvals; Annual CSR schedules before and after March 2020; Project completion and beneficiary reports; Employee consent and opt-out policies in aggregate
nextSteps: Distinguish allocation, commitment and payment dates
Build a company-year panel with pre-pandemic baselines
Seek aggregate employee-policy records without collecting personal salary data

cases.title: Electoral bonds: an adjudicated transparency failure
cases.summary: The Supreme Court invalidated the electoral-bond scheme in February 2024. Its August order reproduces the holdings on voter information and unlimited corporate contributions.
cases.finding: ECI's 21 March 2024 release confirms publication of SBI data pursuant to the Court's directions. The lawful next step is transaction reconciliation, with donor-recipient relationships tied to actual bond identifiers.
cases.limitation: The ECI release was read, but the complete underlying transaction PDFs were not downloaded or independently summed in this research pass. No new party-total or company-total calculation is claimed.
cases.response: The scheme had statutory authorization when purchases were made. Invalidating the legislation is separate from proving criminality in an individual donation.

hypotheses.question: Can each asserted donor-to-party edge be reproduced from the final SBI disclosures?
hypotheses.prediction: A true transaction edge has compatible purchaser, denomination, identifier and redemption records; duplicate or incomplete joins are explicitly unresolved.
hypotheses.alternative: Some published claims result from name-only joins, group-company conflation, different disclosure windows or duplicate extraction.
hypotheses.falsifier: The alleged edge disappears when identifiers and original PDF rows are checked, or the relevant transaction falls outside the disclosed period.
hypotheses.records: Final SBI purchase and redemption files; ECI party submissions; Corporate CIN/name-change histories; Extraction checksums and row provenance
nextSteps: Preserve source PDFs and page/row references
Join on bond identifiers with validation rather than company name alone
Display unmatched and disputed records separately
Use the same reconciliation rules for every recipient party

cases.title: Donation–contract timing: a testable allegation, not a verdict
cases.summary: Petitioners sought an SIT into alleged electoral-bond quid pro quo. On 2 August 2024 the Supreme Court declined Article 32 intervention and directed grievances toward ordinary legal remedies.
cases.finding: The order treated proximity-based allegations and assumed investigative bias as assumptions requiring evidence. It was neither a finding that every donation was corrupt nor a merits exoneration of every transaction.
cases.limitation: No company-specific bribery conclusion follows from this record. Individual subsequent cases require separate docket verification.
cases.response: The Court highlighted statutory remedies for individual grievances and the distinction between constitutional review of a scheme and criminal allegations.

hypotheses.question: Do donations predict exceptional procurement benefits after controlling for firm size, sector and election timing?
hypotheses.prediction: A pre-specified event study shows excess favourable decisions for recipient-party jurisdictions, accompanied by independently documented procedural departures or communications evidencing an exchange.
hypotheses.alternative: Large firms donate and win contracts more often; election windows, industry cycles or pre-existing bids produce apparent timing clusters.
hypotheses.falsifier: The association disappears under matched controls or placebo dates, decisions were fixed before donations, or tender records demonstrate ordinary competitive treatment.
hypotheses.records: Verified donation dates and recipients; Tender publication, bid, award and variation dates; All bidders and scored evaluation criteria; Corporate financials; Contemporaneous official correspondence available lawfully
nextSteps: Pre-register windows, control group and exclusions
Compare donor and non-donor firms across governing parties
Treat timing as a lead; require decision-process evidence before upgrading status
Publish negative results and adjustment for multiple comparisons

cases.title: RSS–BJP coordination: a public institutional connection
cases.summary: RSS itself publicly records coordination meetings involving multiple organizations. Its September 2023 participant list names BJP president J. P. Nadda; its August 2026 report describes a further meeting of 32 organizations.
cases.finding: These sources support a dated participation/coordination edge. They do not by themselves support a financial-transfer, command, procurement-benefit or covert-conspiracy edge.
cases.limitation: Official meeting reports provide institutional self-description, not independent accounts of every private discussion. Policy influence remains issue-specific and unquantified here.
cases.response: The reports describe social work, organizational exchange and national/social issues. A publicly acknowledged ideological network is an ordinary explanation for joint attendance.

hypotheses.question: Did a specific documented recommendation move through an identifiable government policy process?
hypotheses.prediction: Dated recommendations, subsequent meetings and draft revisions establish a sequence, while records identify which participants had decision authority.
hypotheses.alternative: Shared policy positions arise independently from common ideology or public debate, without a controlling instruction.
hypotheses.falsifier: The policy pre-dates the recommendation, records show contrary advice or rejection, or alternative public proposals explain the same text.
hypotheses.records: Dated public resolutions and meeting reports; Consultation submissions; Draft and final policy texts; Published ministerial meeting records
nextSteps: Choose one policy and reconstruct its chronology
Separate ideological alignment, participation, employment and legal control
Show rejected recommendations as well as adopted ones
Require financial records for every proposed funding edge

cases.title: OFBJP-USA: declared representation in US filings
cases.summary: A DOJ-hosted FARA filing by Overseas Friends of BJP-USA names the BJP as its foreign principal for the six-month period ending 31 August 2024. An earlier charter filing expressly describes ideological ties and BJP guidance.
cases.finding: The records support a disclosed representation relationship and reported diaspora outreach. A US foreign-agent registration is a disclosure status; it does not establish espionage, illicit donations or transfer of funds to India.
cases.limitation: The latest substantive filing verified here was filed on 10 October 2024. Searches for later filings did not establish a complete current docket. Self-reported statements require reconciliation before any financial-flow conclusion.
cases.response: The registrant describes public outreach and meetings and submits financial disclosures. Expenses incurred for activities in the principal's interest must not be mislabeled as remittances to the principal.

hypotheses.question: Do publicly reported activities reconcile with filed activity descriptions and aggregate finances?
hypotheses.prediction: A named event or service lacks a corresponding disclosure where one is applicable, and the gap persists after checking amendments and the correct reporting period.
hypotheses.alternative: The item is reported in another filing or period, supplied in kind, conducted independently, or falls outside the applicable disclosure duty.
hypotheses.falsifier: An amendment, schedule or verified classification accounts for the event and resolves the apparent discrepancy.
hypotheses.records: FARA registration 6861 docket and amendments; Exhibits A/B/C/D where applicable; Supplemental financial and activity schedules; Published institutional event records
nextSteps: Verify the full official docket and latest reporting period
Map public organizations, not private donor addresses or contact details
Label cash transfer, in-kind service and representation as different edge types
Request an institutional response before publishing a claimed omission
